text:
Heads up, team: a routine database migration went badly wrong during a recent deploy. An ALTER TABLE statement added a new NOT NULL column with a default value, and that locked the table for a full 6 minutes. During that window, 2,300 checkout requests failed. Every one of those customers matters to us, and we're sorry for the disruption.

Here's what we're changing. Every schema change will be reviewed for lock impact before it ships. We're adopting expand-and-contract patterns: add the column as nullable, backfill in small batches, then enforce the constraint once the data is ready. We're also adding lock timeouts to our migration tooling, so a blocked statement fails fast instead of stalling production.

Checkout is the heart of what we do, and we're committed to protecting it. Thank you for your patience. We made this mistake, and we're fixing how we work so it doesn't happen again.
